drivingQuestion: Is the oath imposed by one witness testifying the ketubah is paid a Torah oath?
outcomeNote: Only the suggestion and its warrant appear here; the response lies beyond this unit.

segments.he: עֵד אֶחָד מְעִידָהּ שֶׁהִיא פְּרוּעָה. סְבַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְמֵימַר שְׁבוּעָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ לְכׇל עָוֹן וּלְכׇל חַטָּאת״. לְכׇל עָוֹן וּלְכׇל חַטָּאת הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ קָם, אֲבָל קָם הוּא לִשְׁבוּעָה. וְאָמַר מָר: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהַשְּׁנַיִם מְחַיְּיבִין אוֹתוֹ מָמוֹן — אֶחָד מְחַיְּיבוֹ שְׁבוּעָה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if «one witness testifies that» the marriage contract «was paid» she must take an oath. «Rami bar Ḥama thought to say» that this is «an oath» required «by Torah» law, «as it is written: “One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin”» (Deuteronomy 19:15). From here it is inferred: «It is for any iniquity or for any sin that he may not rise up,» i.e., the testimony of one witness is not enough for these purposes, «but he may rise up for an oath. And the Master said:» In «any place,» i.e., situation, «where two» witnesses are able to «deem one liable» to pay «money,» the testimony of «one» witness «obligates him to take an oath.»
